claims.text: Bigelow said in August 1998 that anomalous aerial activity and unusual animal deaths had continued on and around the property: 'We wouldn't be there just for the weather.'

claims.text: As a condition of the 1996 purchase the Shermans agreed to keep quiet about what they had witnessed on the property.

edges.label: Kelleher was NIDS deputy administrator and ran field operations
edges.note: Kelleher managed the ranch instrumentation, the necropsy response programme and the hotline casework for the institute's whole life.

edges.label: Puthoff was among the consultants Bigelow hired at NIDS in 1995
edges.note: The New Yorker records that among the consultants Bigelow hired was Hal Puthoff, 'whose work in paranormal studies dated back decades, to Project Stargate.'

edges.label: Vallee served on the NIDS advisory board
edges.note: Vallee had been at SRI in the 1970s and had documented deliberate human disinformation in UFO cases from 1979 - the phenomenon later confirmed in the Bennewitz affair.

edges.label: Alexander sat on the NIDS board from its founding
edges.note: Alexander brought Los Alamos and Army INSCOM programme experience and had previously convened a cleared interagency canvass for a compartmented UFO effort.

edges.label: NIDS headquarters 1995-2004
edges.note: The National Institute for Discovery Science was established in 1995 by Robert T. Bigelow, described in contemporary reporting as a Las Vegas-based millionaire philanthropist and real estate developer, and it investigated both aerial phenomena and the survival of consciousness after death, running a reporting hotline and commissioning veterinary necropsies on animal-mutilation reports. It is the direct institutional predecessor of the BAASS staffing that later executed AAWSAP. Tier 2: the source places Bigelow in Las Vegas rather than stating NIDS's own registered address.

edges.label: NIDS operated a permanently instrumented field station at the ranch
edges.note: Bigelow moved in a research team, surveillance equipment and full-time caretakers immediately after the purchase.

edges.label: founded and privately funded NIDS 1995-2004
edges.note: NIDS described itself as a privately funded science institute studying aerial phenomena and animal mutilations; Bigelow shut it down in 2004.

edges.label: purchased the ranch in 1996 and owned it throughout the DIA contract
edges.note: The Deseret News reported the sale in June 1996 and Bigelow confirmed in August 1998 that the Shermans had agreed as a condition of purchase to keep quiet about what they had witnessed.
